heatmap.title: Therapeutic Window Planner
heatmap.subtitle: Pre-hardware decision map, click any point to navigate there
heatmap.tipCanvas: Therapeutic Window Planner X = RF Frequency (log) · Y = Field Intensity ■ Green Selective target lysis, healthy safe ■ Amber Marginal, healthy stressed ■ Red Ablative, non-selective (avoid) ■ Orange Thermal ≥ 42°C ■ Cyan Approaching window · ■ Dark Sub-threshold Lines: yellow dashed = optimal freq · cyan dotted = fc corners Click to set operating point.
heatmap.tipStats: Operating Point Statistics All values are computed at the current frequency and field using the Schwan single-shell model (or resonance Lorentzian in resonance mode). T-DR: disruption ratio of target cell = Vm_T × PEF / Vm_thr_T H-DR: disruption ratio of healthy cell = Vm_H × PEF / Vm_thr_H H-Temp: healthy cell steady-state temperature = 37 + SAR·dc / (λ·cp) P(lysis): fraction of randomly-oriented target cells that exceed lysis threshold P = max(0, 1 − 1/DR) , from 3D isotropic cosθ distribution Selectivity: TI = DR_T / DR_H (capped at 99.9) All values update live as you drag the sliders.
heatmap.tipOptLine: Optimal Selectivity Frequency Vertical yellow dashed line shows the frequency that maximises TI = DR_T/DR_H. For mammalian cells: found by a 300-point log scan (10 kHz-500 MHz). For bacteria/virus in resonance mode: f_res of the capsid/cell-wall. Click ⭐ Snap to optimal to navigate to this frequency.
heatmap.tipFcLines: Corner Frequency Markers (fc) Vertical cyan dotted lines show the Schwan characteristic frequencies: fc = 1/(2πτ), τ = R·Cm·(2σ_e+σ_i)/(2σ_e·σ_i) Below fc: Vm ≈ Vm_max (quasi-DC maximum, highest disruption ratio). Above fc: Vm ∝ 1/f, exponential roll-off, DR falls. For maximum selectivity, operate below both fc markers.
heatmap.tipFresLine: Resonant Frequency Marker (f_res) Vertical white dashed line shows the acoustic capsid/cell-wall resonant frequency. f_res ≈ v_shell / (2R) (Tsen et al. 2007; Dykeman & Sankey 2010) The resonance peak width is set by the Q-factor (peptidoglycan/capsid damping). Lower Q → broader but weaker peak. Higher Q → narrow spike, high selectivity.
heatmap.tipPLysis: P(lysis), Random Orientation Fraction In a real experiment, cells are randomly oriented in 3D. The Schwan Vm has a cosθ factor: Vm(θ) = Vm_max · |cosθ|. For a 3D isotropic distribution: P = max(0, 1 − 1/DR) At DR=1.0: only the perfectly-aligned pole lyses → P = 0% At DR=2.0: 50% of cells lyse At DR=5.0: 80% of cells lyse Resonance mode: acoustic pressure is omnidirectional, cosθ does not apply.
heatmap.tipHoverZone: Hovered Point Physics computed with current protocol settings (medium, waveform, dc, pulse width). Click to navigate to this operating point.
heatmap.tipRegime: Frequency Regime at Operating Point Determines the hardware required for field delivery. Electrolytic (<300 MHz): direct-contact cuvette + pulse generator Near-field RF (300 MHz-1 GHz): 50 Ω coaxial probe + RF amplifier Microwave (>1 GHz): rectangular waveguide or resonant cavity
heatmap.tipSkinDepth: EM Penetration Depth at Operating Point Exact lossy-dielectric formula: δ = 1/α, α = ω√(με/2)×√(√(1+(σ/ωε)²)−1) (Gabriel et al. 1996; good-conductor approx. only valid below ~300 MHz in saline) Saline: 100 MHz→48 mm · 1 GHz→32 mm · ε_r decreases above 1 GHz (Cole-Cole) Sets the usable sample depth: ≥20 mm: full cuvette penetration 5-20 mm: cm-depth; outer layer accessible <5 mm: near-surface only; waveguide or cavity coupling required
